no: Contributed by Clark Kimberling and Peter Moses. January 20, 2026.

Suppose P = \(p : q : r\) and U = \(u : v : w\) are points (barycentric coordinates), and define the chi-point of P and U, denoted by χ(P,U), as follows: χ(P,U) = p*(v^2 + w^2) : q*(w^2 + u^2) : r*(u:^2 + v^2)
Geometrically, * χ(P,U) = crosspoint[P, P / U^2] * χ(P,U) = crosssum[gP, U^2 tP*X_6], where gP = isogonal conjugate of P, and tP = isotomic conjugate of P
Define the theta-point of P and U, denoted by ϑ(P,U), as follows: ϑ(P,U) = u*(q*v + r*w) : v*(r*w + p*u) : w*(p*u + q*v)
Geometrically, f(P,U) is the intersection of PU and the trilinear polar of the isotomic conjugate of U.
For more, see the preamble just before X_71316.
